title: Put a book on its stand and turn the marked page
instruction: Pick the green book up with both arms and set it on the wooden reading stand. Open its cover, turn the blue-marked page, and release the book.
context: A reader wants to resume from a marked place. Preparing the book on a stand makes the page available for reading hands-free.
setup: A closed green notebook made of cloth-backed cardboard and paper lies flat beside an empty wooden stand. Its body measures 167 × 225 × 34 mm. It has two cloth carry tabs and a blue 34 × 18 × 3 mm paper marker. The stand has a 326 × 256 × 28 mm plinth, a raised support for the open cover, and four 14 mm wide locating stops. They sit on a 580 × 870 × 40 mm wooden table. Two YAM arms face the table. The README specifies the exact reset coordinates.
scoring: For the final 20 controls, award 0.35 when the released spine stays within 16 mm horizontally and 10 mm vertically of the stand datum and tilts at most 9 degrees. Add 0.30 when the released cover opens at least 150 degrees. Add 0.35 when the released marked page also turns at least 150 degrees. Each credited part must have at most 0.1 N of gripper contact.
reset_notes: Use seed 0, close both book panels and place the free book flat to the right of the empty stand as seen in the setup image. Start both arms in their neutral poses.
fidelity: The book is free to move, and its cover and marked leaf turn through physical grip and contact. The marked leaf is a rigid paper proxy with a reinforced tab. The remaining bound pages form a single block. The stand has physical locating guides and supports the open cover.
